title: MicroWorld: Empowering Multimodal Large Language Models to Bridge the Microscopic Domain Gap with Multimodal Attributed Property Graph
claim: Existing retrieval paradigms each lack key capabilities; ours is the only one combining language model, multimodal, graph, and domain knowledge.
layout: 5 side-by-side columns, top-to-bottom flow, checkmark/cross checklist at bottom
description: Five vertical color-coded panels sit side by side: Text-Centric (blue), Vision-Centric (green), Text-Vision-Centric (orange), Graph-Centric (purple) and MAPG-Centric (Ours, brown/gray). Each panel has a title pill at the top. Below it is the same user query, a microscopy image with the text 'What's the microscopy modality used to acquire this image?'. An arrow leads to a retrieval step, shown as a search icon, an image+book icon pair, a graph of nodes, or a microscope with a knowledge graph. Each panel ends in a 'Context' box that lists ranked items (Caption, Image, Image+Caption, Knowledge), then a brain icon. A checklist of LLM, Multimodal, Graph and Knowledge, marked with red crosses or green ticks, closes each panel. The final panel has the most green ticks, and the eye is drawn to it by its distinct styling.
caption: Comparison with prior RAG paradigms. While Text-Centric , Vision-Centric , and Text-Vision-Centric methods rely respectively on captions, images, or a multimodal combination of both, Graph-Centric RAG builds a caption-based structured graph but lacks domain-specific modeling. Conversely, our MAPG-Centric approach is tailored for biological microscopy and naturally integrates visual modalities. LLM: Utilization of a Large Language Model. Multimodal: Use of multimodal features during retrieval. Graph: Construction of a structured retrieval space. Knowledge: Provision of specialized biological microscopy knowledge.
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show remarkable potential for scientific reasoning, yet their performance in specialized domains such as microscopy remains limited by the scarcity of domain-specific training data and the difficulty of encoding fine-grained expert knowledge into model parameters. To bridge the gap, we introduce MicroWorld, a framework for structured-knowledge augmentation with a complementary visual retrieval pathway, using a multimodal attributed property graph (MAPG) without domain-specific fine-tuning. MicroWorld extracts biomedical entities and relations via scispaCy or LLM-based triplet mining, aligns images and entities in a shared embedding space using Qwen3-VL-Embedding, and assembles a knowledge graph comprising approximately 106K nodes and 2.62M typed edges spanning eight relation categories. At inference time, a graph-augmented retrieval pipeline matches query entities to the MAPG and injects structured knowledge context into the MLLM prompt. On MicroVQA, MicroWorld raises Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct accuracy from 48.8% to 67.1% (+18.3 percentage points; 37.5% relative), exceeding zero-shot GPT-5 (59.4%). The identical retrieved context raises GPT-5 to 71.5%, and GPT-5's own entity extraction reaches 73.3%. On MicroBench, 8B Single-Pass improves overall accuracy by 4.0 percentage points. The benefits are greatest for knowledge-intensive reasoning; fine-grained visual discrimination and the additional visual-pathway contribution remain limited. Code and accompanying resources: https://github.com/ieellee/MicroWorld.
